Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.values

Class MandelaIterator

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.values.MandelaIterator
public final class MandelaIterator extends Object
The cursor a for loop drives.

One object covers lists, maps, ranges, strings and enum constants, so the machine needs a single trio of opcodes — NEW_ITER, ITER_NEXT and ITER_VALUE — instead of a specialised loop shape per container. The cursor is deliberately advance then peek: advance() moves to the next element and reports whether there was one, and the element stays available until the next advance, which is what lets a destructuring body read the same element twice without the iterator having to support look-back.

A map iterates its keys, so for (k in map) reads the way a Java keySet() loop does; for ((k, v) in map) asks the machine for the key/value pair through key() and value().

Not thread-safe, and it reflects the container as it is: mutating a list while looping it moves the cursor over the new contents, exactly as a java.util.Iterator would.
